The work_authorization product has everify_case_number as a plain attribute — a denormalization signal. Li

attributes.name: case_closure_date
attributes.description: The date on which the E-Verify case was officially closed in the federal portal. Marks the end of the case lifecycle. Used for compliance reporting, audit trails, and calculating case processing duration.

attributes.name: case_closure_reason
attributes.description: The business reason for closing the E-Verify case. Captures whether closure was due to authorization, final nonconfirmation, early termination, case error, or other administrative reasons. Required for federal audit trails and DOL regulatory reporting.
attributes.value_regex: Employment Authorized|Final Nonconfirmation|Employee Terminated Prior to Resolution|Case Error|Duplicate Case|Other

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the E-Verify case as returned by the DHS/SSA federal portal. Drives compliance workflow actions including TNC resolution, referral, and closure processes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Employment Authorized|Tentative Nonconfirmation|Final Nonconfirmation|Case in Continuance|Closed|DHS Verification in Process — promote to reference product]
attributes.value_regex: Employment Authorized|Tentative Nonconfirmation|Final Nonconfirmation|Case in Continuance|Closed

attributes.name: case_verification_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of E-Verify verification being performed. New Hire cases are standard; Rehire cases apply when a worker is rehired after a break in service; Federal Contractor cases apply under FAR E-Verify clause requirements for federal contract placements.

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance officers to document case-specific notes, exceptions, escalations, or remediation actions taken during the E-Verify process. Used for internal audit documentation and legal hold purposes. Sourced from Sterling BGC and manual compliance team entries.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this E-Verify case record was first created in the Staffing Hr compliance data platform (Silver Layer). Represents the data ingestion audit trail timestamp, distinct from the case submission timestamp. Required for SOC 2 Type II audit controls.

attributes.name: dhs_case_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Department of Homeland Security (DHS) E-Verify Case Number
attributes.description: The official case number assigned by the DHS/SSA E-Verify federal portal upon case creation. This is the externally-known identifier used to track and reference the case with federal authorities. Sourced from Sterling BGC and E-Verify federal portal integration.

attributes.name: document_title_list_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker presented a List A document (establishes both identity and employment authorization) or a combination of List B (identity) and List C (employment authorization) documents during I-9 verification. Relevant to E-Verify case processing rules.

attributes.name: employee_first_day_of_work
attributes.description: The date the employee began work for pay at Staffing Hr or the client site. E-Verify cases must be submitted within 3 business days of this date per federal program rules. Used to validate timely submission compliance.

attributes.name: employer_case_creator
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the Staffing Hr staff member (recruiter, onboarding specialist, or compliance officer) who created and submitted the E-Verify case. Required for internal audit trails and accountability tracking per SOC 2 Type II controls.

attributes.name: employment_authorization_expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiration date of the workers employment authorization document as recorded in the E-Verify case. Triggers re-verification requirements for workers with temporary employment authorization. Critical for ongoing compliance monitoring and assignment management.

attributes.name: federal_closure_code
attributes.description: The standardized federal closure code assigned by the DHS E-Verify portal upon case closure. Used for regulatory reporting, federal audit reconciliation, and compliance tracking with DHS and DOL requirements.

attributes.name: federal_contractor_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this E-Verify case was submitted under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) E-Verify clause requirement for federal contractor placements. True = federal contractor case; False = standard commercial placement. Drives OFCCP compliance reporting.

attributes.name: final_case_result
attributes.description: The conclusive result of the E-Verify case after all resolution steps (TNC contest, referral, continuance) have been completed. Used for final compliance determination and regulatory reporting to DOL and EEOC.

attributes.name: further_action_notice_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: E-Verify Further Action Notice (FAN) Issuance Date
attributes.description: The date on which the Further Action Notice (FAN) was provided to the worker. Must be documented as part of the TNC resolution process. Null when no FAN was issued. Used for compliance audit trails and DOL regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: further_action_notice_issued
attributes.business_glossary_term: E-Verify Further Action Notice (FAN) Issued Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Further Action Notice (FAN) was issued to the worker as part of the TNC process. True = FAN was issued and provided to the worker; False = no FAN issued. Required documentation step for TNC compliance per DHS E-Verify program rules.

attributes.name: initial_case_result
attributes.description: The first result returned by the E-Verify system upon initial case submission. Distinct from the final case status — captures the original determination before any TNC resolution or continuance. Key field for compliance audit trails required by DOL and IRS.
attributes.value_regex: Employment Authorized|Tentative Nonconfirmation|DHS Verification in Process|SSA Tentative Nonconfirmation

attributes.name: late_submission_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the E-Verify case was submitted after the federally mandated 3-business-day window from the employees first day of work. True = late submission; False = timely submission. Used for compliance monitoring, SLA reporting, and DOL audit risk management.

attributes.name: photo_match_result
attributes.description: The result of the E-Verify photo matching step, where the photo on the workers identity document is compared against DHS records. Applicable when the worker presents a document with a photo that E-Verify can match. Used for fraud detection and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: re_verification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the workers employment authorization requires re-verification before the expiry date. True = re-verification is required; False = no re-verification needed (e.g., U.S. citizen). Drives compliance workflow alerts for assignment managers.

attributes.name: referral_agency
attributes.description: The federal agency (Social Security Administration or Department of Homeland Security) to which the worker was referred to resolve a Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC). Determines the resolution process and timeline. Null or None when no referral was required.

attributes.name: referral_date
attributes.description: The date on which the worker was referred to the SSA or DHS to resolve a Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC). Must occur within the federally mandated timeframe after TNC issuance. Null when no TNC referral was required. Tracked for DOL and DHS audit compliance.

attributes.name: referral_deadline_date
attributes.description: The federally mandated deadline by which the worker must be referred to SSA or DHS to contest a Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC). Calculated from the TNC issuance date per DHS E-Verify program rules. Used for SLA monitoring and compliance alerting.

attributes.name: resolution_deadline_date
attributes.description: The federally mandated deadline by which the TNC must be resolved by the referring agency (SSA or DHS). Staffing Hr must not terminate employment before this date solely due to TNC status. Tracked for EEOC anti-discrimination compliance and DOL audit.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this E-Verify case record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation between Sterling Background Check integration and the DHS E-Verify federal portal.

attributes.name: sterling_case_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Sterling Background Check (BGC) E-Verify Case Reference
attributes.description: The case reference number assigned by Sterling Background Check system for this E-Verify submission. Used for reconciliation between Sterling BGC integration records and the DHS E-Verify federal portal. Enables cross-system audit trail.

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the E-Verify case was submitted to the DHS/SSA federal portal. This is the principal business event timestamp for the case. Must occur within 3 business days of the employees first day of work per federal E-Verify program rules.

attributes.name: tnc_issuance_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC) was issued by the E-Verify system. Triggers the mandatory referral and resolution timeline. Null when no TNC was issued. Critical for calculating referral and resolution deadlines.

attributes.name: tnc_resolution_status
attributes.description: Tracks the workers response and resolution outcome for a Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC). Indicates whether the worker contested the TNC, did not contest, and the resulting resolution. Null when no TNC was issued. Required for OFCCP and DOL compliance audit trails.

attributes.name: tnc_type
attributes.description: Identifies whether the Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC) was issued by the Social Security Administration (SSA), the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or both. Null or None when no TNC was issued. Drives the appropriate referral agency and resolution workflow.
attributes.value_regex: SSA TNC|DHS TNC|SSA and DHS TNC|None

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this E-Verify case record was last modified in the Staffing Hr compliance data platform. Tracks all status changes, TNC updates, and closure events for audit trail purposes. Required for SOC 2 Type II and DOL audit compliance.

attributes.name: worker_contested_tnc
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker chose to contest the Tentative Nonconfirmation (TNC) with the issuing agency (SSA or DHS). True = worker contested; False = worker did not contest. Null when no TNC was issued. Critical for FLSA and EEOC anti-discrimination compliance.

attributes.description: Indicates whether the state-level ABC Test (stricter than IRS Common Law Test) applies to this classification determination based on the work jurisdiction. True = ABC Test governs; False = IRS Common Law or DOL Economic Realities Test applies.

attributes.name: abc_test_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the ABC Test evaluation where applicable. Pass = worker qualifies as independent contractor under all three prongs; Fail = worker must be classified as W-2 employee; Not Applicable = ABC Test does not govern this jurisdiction.

attributes.name: behavioral_control_score
attributes.description: Numeric score (0–100) reflecting the degree of behavioral control the staffing firm or client exercises over the worker, per the IRS Common Law Test. Higher scores indicate greater control and stronger W-2 classification support.

attributes.name: classification_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for this classification determination record, used in audit correspondence, legal filings, and IRS inquiries. Format: WC-YYYY-NNNNNN.

attributes.name: classification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this classification determination. Pending = under review; Active = in force; Superseded = replaced by a newer determination; Appealed = under formal challenge; Revoked = withdrawn due to error or legal order.

attributes.name: classification_type
attributes.description: The determined classification type for the worker engagement. W2 = W-2 employee (temporary or permanent); 1099_IC = Independent Contractor (1099-MISC); 1099_NEC = Non-Employee Compensation contractor; C2C = Corp-to-Corp engagement; EOR = Employer of Record arrangement. This is the SSOT for IC vs. W-2 decisions.

attributes.name: client_requested_classification
attributes.description: The worker classification type explicitly requested by the client in the job order, MSA, or SOW. May differ from the compliance-determined classification. Used to track client preference vs. legal determination and flag misalignment.

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance officers or legal counsel to document additional observations, risk factors, remediation actions, or contextual information relevant to this classification determination. Retained for audit trail.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this worker classification record was first created in the system. Audit trail field required for DOL, IRS, and SOC 2 compliance.

attributes.name: determination_basis
attributes.description: The legal or regulatory test framework used to arrive at the classification determination. Behavioral Control = IRS test on instruction/training; Financial Control = IRS test on investment/profit/loss; Relationship Type = IRS test on written contracts/benefits/permanency; ABC Test = state-level test (e.g., California AB5); Economic Realities = DOL FLSA test; Multi-Factor = combination of tests applied.

attributes.name: determination_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal worker classification determination was made and recorded. This is the principal business event date for this record.

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: The date from which this classification determination is binding and in effect for the worker engagement. May differ from determination_date if retroactive or prospective.

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: The date on which this classification determination expires or is superseded. Null for open-ended classifications. Populated when a new determination replaces this one or the engagement ends.

attributes.name: financial_control_score
attributes.description: Numeric score (0–100) reflecting the degree of financial control the staffing firm or client exercises over the worker, per the IRS Common Law Test. Considers investment in tools, opportunity for profit/loss, and services available to the general market.

attributes.name: flsa_exemption_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) Exemption Status
attributes.description: FLSA overtime exemption classification for W-2 employees. Non-Exempt = entitled to overtime pay; Exempt categories follow the FLSA white-collar exemption tests (Executive, Administrative, Professional, Highly Compensated, Outside Sales). Drives OT and DT pay rule application. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: non_exempt|exempt_executive|exempt_administrative|exempt_professional|exempt_highly_compensated|exempt_outside_sales — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ic_agreement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Independent Contractor Agreement was executed. Used to verify agreement predates the engagement start and is current for the classification period.

attributes.name: ic_agreement_on_file
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent Contractor (IC) Agreement on File Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a signed Independent Contractor Agreement is on file for this worker engagement. Required for 1099/IC classifications. Absence of a signed agreement increases misclassification risk.

attributes.name: irs_audit_exposure_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing compliance officer or attorney notes regarding IRS audit exposure risk for this classification. Documents specific factors that could attract IRS scrutiny, misclassification penalties, or back-tax liability under IRC Section 3509.

attributes.name: misclassification_risk_level
attributes.description: Overall assessed risk level that the current classification determination could be challenged or reversed by the IRS, DOL, or state labor authority. Drives compliance monitoring frequency and legal review escalation.

attributes.name: nda_on_file
attributes.description: Indicates whether a signed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) is on file for this worker engagement. Tracked as part of the compliance documentation package for the classification record.

attributes.name: non_compete_on_file
attributes.description: Indicates whether a signed Non-Compete Agreement is on file for this worker. Relevant to classification because non-compete clauses are more consistent with employee relationships and may affect IC classification defensibility.

attributes.name: override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the final classification determination overrides the system-recommended or compliance-officer-recommended classification. True = an override was applied; False = determination follows standard process. Triggers mandatory documentation and senior review.

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation documenting the business or legal justification for overriding the standard classification recommendation. Required when override_flag is True. Retained for audit trail and IRS inquiry response.

attributes.name: previous_classification_type
attributes.description: The prior classification type for this worker on this engagement, captured when a reclassification event occurs. Enables audit trail of classification changes and supports IRS back-period liability analysis.

attributes.name: reclassification_date
attributes.description: Date on which a workers classification was changed from a prior type to the current classification_type. Null if this is the original classification with no prior change.

attributes.name: reclassification_trigger
attributes.description: The event or authority that triggered a reclassification of the worker. Captures whether the change was driven by an IRS audit, DOL investigation, state labor audit, client request, proactive internal compliance review, legal counsel advice, or court order. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: irs_audit|dol_audit|state_audit|client_request|internal_review|legal_counsel|court_order — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: relationship_type_score
attributes.description: Numeric score (0–100) reflecting the nature of the relationship between the worker and the engaging party, per the IRS Common Law Test. Considers written contracts, employee benefits, permanency of relationship, and integral business activity.

attributes.name: reviewing_officer_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reviewing Compliance Officer or Attorney Name
attributes.description: Full name of the compliance officer, HR attorney, or legal counsel who reviewed and approved this classification determination. Required for audit trail and regulatory defense.

attributes.name: reviewing_officer_title
attributes.description: Job title or role of the individual who reviewed and approved the classification determination (e.g., Chief Compliance Officer, Employment Attorney, HR Director).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this classification determination originated or was last updated. Supports data lineage and reconciliation across Bullhorn ATS/CRM, SAP SuccessFactors, TempWorks Payroll, Beeline VMS, or manual entry.

attributes.name: ss8_determination_result
attributes.description: The IRSs official determination result from Form SS-8 review. Employee = IRS determined worker is an employee; Independent Contractor = IRS confirmed IC status; Pending = IRS review in progress; Withdrawn = SS-8 filing was withdrawn.

attributes.name: ss8_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether IRS Form SS-8 (Determination of Worker Status for Purposes of Federal Employment Taxes and Income Tax Withholding) has been filed for this worker engagement. True = SS-8 filed with IRS; False = not filed.

attributes.name: ss8_filed_date
attributes.description: Date on which IRS Form SS-8 was filed with the IRS for this worker engagement. Null if ss8_filed is False.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this worker classification record was most recently modified. Audit trail field required for DOL, IRS, and SOC 2 compliance. Tracks reclassification events and override changes.

attributes.name: voluntary_classification_settlement
attributes.business_glossary_term: Voluntary Classification Settlement Program (VCSP) Enrollment Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the staffing firm has enrolled this worker classification under the IRS Voluntary Classification Settlement Program (VCSP), which allows prospective reclassification of workers as employees with reduced tax liability.

attributes.name: workers_comp_exempt
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker is exempt from Workers Compensation coverage based on their classification (e.g., 1099 IC workers are typically exempt). Drives payroll and insurance configuration in TempWorks Payroll.

products.name: eeoc_filing

Supports EEOC and OFCCP audit readiness.

attributes.name: eeoc_filing_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Filing ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each EEOC regulatory filing record in the Staffing Hr compliance system. Primary key for this transactional entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: amended_filing_eeoc_filing_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original EEOC filing record that this amendment supersedes. Populated only when is_amendment is True, enabling amendment history tracking.

attributes.name: client_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_account. Business justification: EEO-1 filings are submitted per employer entity. In co-employment staffing arrangements, the client account is the reporting establishment. Compliance teams must link each EEOC filing to the client ac

attributes.name: contract_msa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.msa. Business justification: MSAs with federal contractors include EEOC/OFCCP compliance obligations. Real business need: MSA-driven filing requirements for federal contractor clients, linking filings to contractual obligations.

attributes.name: job_category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to joborder.job_category. Business justification: EEO-1 Component 1 filings require headcount breakdowns by EEO-1 job category. Linking eeoc_filing to the authoritative job_category record enables regulatory reporting by pulling order/placement data

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.location. Business justification: EEOC multi-establishment reporting requires each filing row to reference a specific client worksite. Staffing firms filing EEO-1 Component 1 for co-employed workers at client locations must link filin

attributes.name: managed_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.managed_program. Business justification: MSP/EOR managed programs are distinct employer-of-record arrangements requiring separate EEOC filings. Compliance teams track EEO-1 submissions by managed program to fulfill program-level federal cont

attributes.name: supplier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.supplier. Business justification: EEO-1 filings in staffing are submitted by the staffing supplier as employer of record. Linking eeoc_filing to the supplier entity enables supplier-level OFCCP/EEOC regulatory reporting, diversity aud

attributes.name: accepted_date
attributes.description: Date on which the EEOC officially accepted and validated this filing submission. Populated when filing_status transitions to accepted. Key date for audit readiness and compliance records.

attributes.name: certifying_official_title
attributes.description: Job title of the company official who certified the EEOC filing. Typically a senior HR, legal, or executive officer with authority to attest to workforce data accuracy.

attributes.name: confirmation_number
attributes.description: Official confirmation number issued by the EEOC upon successful receipt and acceptance of the filing submission. Used for audit readiness and correspondence with the EEOC.

attributes.name: count_american_indian_alaska_native
attributes.business_glossary_term: American Indian or Alaska Native Employee Count
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as American Indian or Alaska Native (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_asian
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as Asian (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_black_african_american
attributes.business_glossary_term: Black or African American Employee Count
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as Black or African American (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_hispanic_latino
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as Hispanic or Latino across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_native_hawaiian_pacific_islander
attributes.business_glossary_term: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander Employee Count
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_two_or_more_races
attributes.business_glossary_term: Two or More Races Employee Count
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as Two or More Races (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: count_white_non_hispanic
attributes.description: Total number of employees self-identified as White (not Hispanic or Latino) across all job categories in this filing. One of the seven EEOC-mandated race/ethnicity categories.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this EEOC filing record was first created in the compliance system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED audit field.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the workforce headcount and demographic data was extracted to populate this EEOC filing. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
attributes.value_regex: SAP SuccessFactors|Bullhorn ATS|Kronos Workforce Ready|Manual Entry|Other

attributes.name: establishment_count
attributes.description: Total number of physical establishments (locations) included in this EEOC filing. Multi-establishment employers must report headcount data for each location.

attributes.name: filing_deadline
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline date by which this EEOC filing must be submitted to remain in compliance. Set annually by the EEOC.

attributes.name: filing_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments entered by the compliance team regarding this EEOC filing. May include explanations for data anomalies, amendment rationale, or internal review observations.

attributes.name: filing_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this EEOC filing submission, used for tracking and correspondence with the EEOC. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.

attributes.name: filing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the EEOC filing submission. Tracks progression from draft preparation through EEOC acceptance or rejection. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this transaction.

attributes.name: filing_year
attributes.description: Calendar year for which this EEOC report is being filed (e.g., 2023). Determines the applicable reporting period and regulatory deadline.

attributes.name: is_amendment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this filing is an amendment to a previously submitted EEOC report. Amendments correct errors or update data in an accepted original filing.

attributes.name: is_federal_contractor
attributes.description: Indicates whether the filing entity is a federal contractor or subcontractor subject to OFCCP regulations and Executive Order 11246, which imposes additional EEO obligations beyond standard EEOC requirements.

attributes.name: is_first_time_filer
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the first EEOC EEO-1 filing submitted by this employer. First-time filers may have different onboarding requirements and EEOC outreach procedures.

attributes.name: ofccp_audit_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) Audit Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this EEOC filing has been flagged for or is subject to an OFCCP compliance audit or review. Enables proactive audit readiness tracking for federal contractor obligations.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Description of the reason provided by the EEOC for rejecting this filing submission. Populated only when filing_status is rejected. Used to guide corrective action and resubmission.

attributes.name: report_component
attributes.description: Specifies the EEO-1 component being filed. Component 1 covers race/ethnicity and gender by job category; Component 2 (historically) covered pay data by race/ethnicity and gender. Relevant for EEO-1 filers.

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the EEOC report form being filed. EEO-1 is the primary form for private employers and federal contractors; other types apply to unions, state/local governments, and educational institutions. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE for this transaction.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the workforce data reporting period covered by this EEOC filing. Defines the close of the window from which the workforce snapshot is drawn.

attributes.name: reporting_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the workforce data reporting period covered by this EEOC filing. Defines the beginning of the window from which the workforce snapshot is drawn.

attributes.name: snapshot_date
attributes.description: The specific pay period date used as the workforce count snapshot for the EEO-1 filing, typically a pay period in October through December of the filing year. Required by EEOC instructions.

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: Method used to submit the EEOC filing to the EEOC. Options include the EEOC online portal, bulk data upload, API integration, or legacy paper submission.

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the EEOC filing was officially submitted to the EEOC portal. Represents the principal real-world business event timestamp (BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP) for this transaction.

attributes.name: total_female_count
attributes.description: Total number of female employees across all job categories and establishments included in this EEOC filing. Required gender dimension for EEO-1 reporting.

attributes.name: total_headcount
attributes.description: Total number of employees across all establishments included in this EEOC filing during the snapshot pay period. Represents the aggregate workforce count reported to the EEOC.

attributes.name: total_male_count
attributes.description: Total number of male employees across all job categories and establishments included in this EEOC filing. Required gender dimension for EEO-1 reporting.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this EEOC filing record was last modified in the compliance system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED audit field.

Supports OSHA 300/300A annual summary reporting.

attributes.name: osha_incident_id

This normalizes osha_citation_number which can be retrieved via JOIN to regulator

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to credentialing.credential_instance. Linking osha_incident to the relevant training_record enables safety compliance managers to

attributes.name: work_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to placement.work_location. Business justification: OSHA 300 log entries are tied to specific work locations (establishments). Staffing firms track incidents by placement work_location for their own OSHA recordkeeping and safety program management. osh

attributes.name: body_part_affected
attributes.description: The specific body part injured or affected by the illness (e.g., lower back, right hand, left knee, eye, head). Required for OSHA Form 301 and used for ergonomic risk analysis and workers comp claim management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: head|neck|back|shoulder|arm|hand|finger|leg|knee|foot|eye|multiple — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: corrective_action
attributes.description: Narrative description of the corrective and preventive actions taken or planned in response to the incident (e.g., retraining, equipment repair, process change, PPE provision, worksite modification). Required for OSHA compliance program documentation and client safety reporting.

attributes.name: corrective_action_completed_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which all corrective and preventive actions were fully implemented and verified. Used to close the incident record and confirm compliance with the corrective action plan.

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: The target completion date by which all corrective and preventive actions identified in the incident investigation must be implemented. Used for compliance tracking and client safety SLA management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this OSHA incident record was first created in the system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for audit trail and data lineage purposes.

attributes.name: days_away_from_work
attributes.description: The number of calendar days the worker was unable to work due to the injury or illness, as counted per OSHA recordkeeping rules (capped at 180 days for OSHA 300 log purposes). Required for OSHA 300 log Column K and DART rate calculation.

attributes.name: days_restricted_duty
attributes.description: The number of calendar days the worker was placed on restricted work activity or job transfer due to the injury or illness, as counted per OSHA recordkeeping rules (capped at 180 days). Required for OSHA 300 log Column L and DART rate calculation.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: The type of event or exposure that directly produced the injury or illness, per BLS Occupational Injury and Illness Classification Manual (OIICS) event categories. Used for trend analysis, root cause classification, and OSHA 300A summary reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fall|struck_by|caught_in|overexertion|exposure|transportation|violence|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: incident_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the workplace injury or illness event occurred. This is the principal real-world event date used for OSHA 300 log entry, workers comp filing deadlines, and annual 300A summary reporting. Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for this transaction.

attributes.name: incident_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of how the injury or illness occurred, including the sequence of events, equipment involved, and environmental conditions. Required for OSHA Form 301 and used for root cause analysis and corrective action planning.

attributes.name: incident_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the incident (e.g., INC-2024-000123). Used in OSHA 300 log entries, workers comp filings, client communications, and regulatory correspondence. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.

attributes.name: incident_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the OSHA incident record. open indicates active investigation; under_review indicates pending recordability determination; closed indicates fully resolved with corrective actions documented; appealed indicates contested recordability; voided indicates duplicate or erroneous entry.

attributes.name: incident_time
attributes.description: The time of day (HH:MM, 24-hour format) at which the workplace incident occurred. Used for shift-pattern analysis, root cause investigation, and OSHA 300 log documentation.

attributes.name: injury_illness_type
attributes.description: OSHA-defined classification of the nature of the workplace injury or illness. Maps directly to the OSHA Form 300 column headers: injury, skin disorder, respiratory condition, poisoning, hearing loss, or all other illness. Required for OSHA 300 log and 300A annual summary.

attributes.name: injury_nature
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific nature of the injury or illness (e.g., laceration, fracture, sprain, burn, contusion, amputation, concussion). Provides granularity beyond the OSHA Form 300 type classification for root cause analysis and trend reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: laceration|fracture|sprain|strain|burn|contusion|amputation|concussion|puncture|abrasion|dislocation|crush_injury — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: investigation_completed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal incident investigation was completed and the investigation report was finalized. Used to track investigation timeliness and ensure compliance with internal safety program SLAs.

attributes.name: is_fatality
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident resulted in the death of the worker. True = fatality. Triggers mandatory OSHA reporting within 8 hours of employer knowledge under 29 CFR Part 1904.39 and activates escalation protocols.

attributes.name: is_hospitalized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker was admitted to a hospital (inpatient) as a result of the incident. True = inpatient hospitalization. Triggers mandatory OSHA reporting within 24 hours under 29 CFR Part 1904.39.

attributes.name: is_osha_recordable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident meets OSHA recordability criteria under 29 CFR Part 1904.7 (i.e., results in days away from work, restricted duty, medical treatment beyond first aid, loss of consciousness, or diagnosis of a significant injury/illness). True = recordable; False = first-aid only. Drives OSHA 300 log entry requirement.

attributes.name: is_privacy_case
attributes.description: Indicates whether this incident qualifies as a privacy case under OSHA recordkeeping rules (e.g., sexual assault, mental illness, HIV/AIDS, needlestick, tuberculosis). True = privacy case. When true, the workers name must be withheld from the OSHA 300 log and replaced with privacy case.

attributes.name: ita_submission_reference
attributes.description: The confirmation identifier returned by OSHAs Injury Tracking Application (ITA) upon electronic submission of the OSHA 300A annual summary data. Required for establishments with 250+ employees or in high-hazard industries under the OSHA Electronic Recordkeeping Rule.

attributes.name: naics_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code
attributes.description: The six-digit NAICS code for the client establishment where the incident occurred. Required for OSHA 300A annual summary and OSHA electronic submission (ITA/OSHA Data Collection) to classify the industry for benchmarking incidence rates.

attributes.name: osha_300_log_entry_number
attributes.description: The sequential entry number assigned to this incident on the OSHA Form 300 (Log of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses) for the applicable calendar year. Required for OSHA 300A annual summary reconciliation and regulatory audit. Null if incident is not recordable.

attributes.name: osha_300_log_year
attributes.description: The calendar year of the OSHA Form 300 log in which this incident is recorded. Used to partition OSHA 300A annual summary reporting and multi-year trend analysis.

attributes.name: osha_report_submitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the required OSHA severe injury report (fatality, amputation, loss of eye, or inpatient hospitalization) has been submitted to OSHA within the mandated timeframe (8 hours for fatalities, 24 hours for other severe injuries).

attributes.name: osha_report_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time at which the OSHA severe injury report was submitted to OSHA (via phone or online). Used to verify compliance with the 8-hour (fatality) and 24-hour (severe injury) reporting deadlines under 29 CFR Part 1904.39.

attributes.name: outcome_type
attributes.description: The most severe outcome classification of the incident per OSHA recordkeeping hierarchy: fatality, days away from work, restricted duty or job transfer, medical treatment beyond first aid, or first aid only. Maps to OSHA Form 300 columns G through J. Drives recordability and severity classification.

attributes.name: recordability_determination_date
attributes.description: The date on which the safety officer or compliance team made the final determination of whether the incident is OSHA recordable. Required for audit trail and to ensure timely OSHA 300 log entry within the 7-calendar-day requirement.

attributes.name: reported_date
attributes.description: The date on which the incident was formally reported to the staffing agency or client safety officer. Used to measure reporting lag compliance against OSHA 24-hour and 8-hour reporting requirements for severe injuries.

attributes.description: Number of client accounts impacted by this regulatory violation. Relevant for systemic violations spanning multiple client engagements (e.g., widespread I-9 non-compliance, multi-site OSHA violations). Supports enterprise-wide compliance risk assessment.

attributes.name: affected_worker_count

attributes.name: agency_case_number

attributes.name: agency_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory agency was formally notified of the violation or initiated contact with the organization. Triggers mandatory response timelines under OSHA, EEOC, and GDPR breach notification requirements. Nullable for violations not yet reported to an agency.

attributes.name: applicable_statute
attributes.description: The specific federal, state, or local statute, regulation, or code section that was violated (e.g., 29 CFR Part 1904, FLSA Section 13(a)(1), Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, INA Section 274A, FCRA Section 604). Supports precise legal tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: board_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the board of directors or executive leadership was formally notified of this regulatory violation. Nullable when board_notification_required is false or notification has not yet occurred. Supports governance audit trails.

attributes.name: board_notification_required

Typically triggered by critical severity, significant financial penalty, or class-action exposure. Supports board-level compliance reporting cadence.

attributes.name: co_employment_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation involves or creates co-employment or joint employment risk between the staffing firm and the client. Triggers enhanced legal review and client notification protocols. Critical for MSP/VMS program compliance and liability management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the regulatory violation record was first created in the compliance system. Supports audit trail requirements mandated by DOL, OSHA, and IRS regulatory frameworks. Distinct from discovery_date which reflects the real-world event time.

attributes.name: data_privacy_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation constitutes or involves a personal data breach requiring notification under GDPR Article 33, CCPA, or FCRA. Triggers the 72-hour GDPR breach notification clock and state-specific breach notification timelines.

attributes.name: discovery_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the regulatory violation was first identified or discovered. Serves as the principal business event date for the violation record. Critical for calculating regulatory response deadlines, statute of limitations tracking, and trending analysis.

attributes.name: discovery_method
attributes.description: The mechanism by which the regulatory violation was identified: internal audit, external complaint, agency notice, whistleblower report, client notification, or self-assessment. Critical for root cause analysis and improving proactive compliance controls.

attributes.name: eeoc_charge_basis

Nullable for non-EEOC violations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: race|color|sex|national_origin|religion|age|disability|genetic_information|retaliation|other — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: financial_penalty_amount

Includes OSHA citations, DOL back-pay orders, EEOC settlements, and IRS tax penalties. Supports financial risk reporting and board-level compliance dashboards.

attributes.name: i9_everify_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation specifically involves I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification or E-Verify non-compliance under the Immigration and Nationality Act. Triggers mandatory ICE/DHS reporting protocols and I-9 audit remediation workflows.

attributes.name: jurisdiction_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the jurisdiction in which the violation occurred (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN). Supports international compliance tracking under GDPR and other cross-border regulatory frameworks for staffing firms with global operations.

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state code (or equivalent jurisdiction identifier) where the violation occurred or where the applicable law is enforced. Supports state labor board reporting, state-specific wage and hour compliance, and CCPA/state privacy law tracking.

attributes.name: legal_counsel_involved
attributes.description: Indicates whether internal or external legal counsel has been engaged in connection with this regulatory violation. Triggers attorney-client privilege protections and routes the record to the legal hold workflow. Required for board-level compliance reporting.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional compliance officer notes, legal observations, or contextual information not captured in structured fields. Supports nuanced documentation of complex multi-framework violations and ongoing investigation details.

attributes.name: ofccp_audit_flag

attributes.name: osha_citation_type

attributes.name: penalty_currency_code

attributes.name: regulatory_body

Drives routing to appropriate legal counsel and determines mandatory response timelines. Includes specific steps, process changes, training requirements, and system corrections required. Supports DOL, OSHA, and EEOC corrective action documentation requirements.

attributes.name: repeat_violation_flag

attributes.name: resolution_status

products.name: audit
products.description: Master record for internal and external compliance audits conducted across the staffing firms operations, with embedded audit finding detail records. Each audit contains one-to-many finding records capturing: finding category (documentation gap, process failure, regulatory breach, control weakness), regulatory citation, affected population size, risk rating (low/medium/high/critical), recommended corrective action, responsible owner, due date, remediation evidence, and closure status. SSOT for all compliance audit activity and finding lifecycle management from identification through closure. Distinct from ofccp_compliance which covers OFCCP-specific federal contractor reviews and Affirmative Action Plans.

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: The date on which the audit was formally closed, meaning all findings have been remediated and accepted by the auditing party. Null if the audit is still open.

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which the formal Corrective Action Plan (CAP) must be submitted to the auditing party or regulatory agency. Drives remediation scheduling and escalation workflows.

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Corrective Action Plan (CAP) associated with this audit. Tracks whether a CAP is required, has been submitted, accepted by the auditing party, rejected, or is overdue.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this compliance audit record was first created in the system. Represents the record audit trail creation point. Sourced from the compliance management platform or manual entry in the Silver layer.

attributes.name: critical_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of findings rated as critical severity within this audit. Critical findings typically require immediate escalation and expedited remediation. Tracked separately for executive and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: estimated_financial_exposure
attributes.description: Estimated monetary exposure or liability associated with the audit findings, expressed in USD. Includes potential penalties, back wages, fines, or remediation costs. Used for financial risk management and executive reporting. Not a calculated aggregate — represents the compliance teams point-in-time risk estimate.

attributes.name: external_auditor_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external auditing firm, regulatory agency, or third-party organization conducting the audit. Null for purely internal audits. Examples: KPMG, Deloitte, DOL Wage and Hour Division, EEOC field office.

attributes.name: fieldwork_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which active audit fieldwork was completed. Marks the transition from evidence gathering to findings analysis and report drafting.

attributes.name: fieldwork_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which active audit fieldwork (evidence collection, interviews, document review) commenced. Represents the principal real-world business event timestamp for the audit engagement start. Used for SLA and TTF (Time to Fill) compliance tracking.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Description of the geographic coverage of the audit, such as specific states, regions, or enterprise-wide. Relevant for state wage and hour audits (SUTA, state FLSA equivalents), CCPA (California), and multi-state compliance reviews.

attributes.name: initiating_agency
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory agency, external auditing firm, or client organization that initiated or requested the audit. Examples: U.S. Department of Labor, EEOC, OSHA, IRS, client legal counsel, or an external CPA firm conducting a SOC 2 review.

attributes.name: lead_auditor_name
attributes.description: Full name of the primary auditor responsible for conducting the audit. May be an internal compliance officer or an external auditor from a regulatory agency or third-party firm. Used for accountability and communication tracking.

attributes.name: legal_counsel_engaged
attributes.description: Indicates whether external or internal legal counsel has been engaged in connection with this audit. True when legal representation is involved, which may affect document privilege and response strategy.

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: The approach used to conduct the audit. Statistical sample audits review a representative subset; full population audits review all records; targeted sample focuses on high-risk records; desk review is document-only; on-site involves physical inspection; hybrid combines methods.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance team notes, observations, or contextual information about the audit that does not fit structured fields. May include background on regulatory context, client relationship considerations, or escalation history.

attributes.name: open_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of audit findings that remain open (not yet remediated or closed) at the time of record update. Supports real-time compliance dashboard monitoring and escalation tracking.

attributes.name: overall_disposition
attributes.description: Final outcome or disposition of the audit. Indicates whether the organization passed, passed with findings requiring remediation, failed, or whether the audit was inconclusive or withdrawn. Key metric for executive compliance dashboards and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: overall_risk_rating
attributes.description: Aggregate risk rating assigned to the audit based on the severity and volume of findings. Rolled up from individual finding risk ratings. Drives escalation protocols and executive reporting. Values: low, medium, high, critical.

attributes.name: period_end_date
attributes.description: The ending date of the time period under audit review. Defines the latest date of business activity or records subject to examination. Together with audit_period_start_date, establishes the audit window.

attributes.name: period_start_date
attributes.description: The beginning date of the time period under audit review. Defines the earliest date of business activity or records subject to examination. Distinct from the audit execution start date.

attributes.name: placement_type_scope
attributes.description: The type of worker placement covered by this audit. Indicates whether the audit applies to temporary workers, permanent placements, contract-to-hire (temp-to-perm), direct hire, SOW (Statement of Work) engagements, or all placement types. Relevant for FLSA worker classification and co-employment risk audits.

attributes.name: prior_audit_reference
attributes.description: Audit number of the most recent prior audit of the same type, used to establish continuity and track repeat findings. Enables year-over-year compliance trend analysis without creating a hard FK dependency at this stage.

attributes.name: privilege_hold_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether attorney-client privilege or work product doctrine has been asserted over audit materials. When True, certain audit documents are restricted from disclosure. Relevant for regulatory audits where legal exposure exists.

attributes.name: regulatory_citation
attributes.description: The primary federal or state regulatory citation, statute, or rule that is the subject of the audit. Examples: 29 CFR Part 516 (FLSA recordkeeping), 8 CFR 274a (I-9), 29 CFR 1904 (OSHA recordkeeping), IRC Section 3509 (worker misclassification). Supports regulatory mapping and citation-level trend analysis.

attributes.name: regulatory_notice_reference
attributes.description: Official case number, docket number, or notice reference assigned by the regulatory agency initiating the audit. Examples: DOL case number, EEOC charge number, IRS examination reference. Used for official correspondence and regulatory tracking.

attributes.name: repeat_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audit contains one or more findings that were also identified in a prior audit cycle (repeat findings). Repeat findings signal systemic control failures and typically result in elevated regulatory scrutiny and penalties.

attributes.name: report_issued_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal audit report (draft or final) was issued to stakeholders. Triggers the remediation clock for findings with regulatory deadlines.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of records, transactions, or workers included in the audit sample. Applicable when audit_methodology is statistical_sample or targeted_sample. Used to calculate deficiency rates and statistical confidence levels.

attributes.name: subtype
